summary: US equities closed higher on Friday and risk appetite recovered after the inflation print: August CPI came in at 3.35% year over year (prior 3.30%) with core at 2.45% (prior 2.47%), and the market has priced a hike for next week's meeting (implied policy rate 4.08% versus an effective fed funds rate of 3.63%). 20 of 22 sectors/themes advanced, led by consumer electronics +4.95%, networking +3.58% and AI infrastructure +3.18%, while only memory -0.35% and the EV supply chain -0.32% fell; AMD rose +2.57% and NVDA was roughly flat at +0.02%. The macro anchor did not loosen, however: the 10-year Treasury yield rose to 4.83% (prior 4.80%) with the real rate at 2.46%, in the 99.6th percentile, and the VIX rose to 17.84 (prior 16.46). The total risk score is 45.21, still caution, with a goldilocks regime and a brief confidence of 0.84.

top_risk_drivers.claim: The real rate and the nominal long yield both sit at historic highs and are the main constraint: the real rate (10-year TIPS) is 2.46% in the 99.6th percentile and the 10-year Treasury yield is 4.83% in the 99.28th percentile, making the macro dimension's 62.19 the highest of the six dimensions.

The August CPI print left a hike fully priced: 3.35% year over year (prior 3.30%) with core at 2.45% (prior 2.47%), and sticky inflation pushed the implied policy rate of 4.08% above the effective fed funds rate of 3.63%.
Volatility rose into the rally: the VIX climbed to 17.84 (prior 16.46), and the volatility dimension scores 31.93 on a rising trend, diverging from the equity advance.
Participation is narrow: semis relative strength is -13.94 and small-cap relative strength -4.12, with the new-highs ratio at only 1.94%, so the index advance is driven largely by thematic sectors.

supporting_signals.claim: Credit markets show no stress: the high-yield OAS is 2.70% (in the 10.93th percentile) and the investment-grade OAS is 0.80%, leaving the liquidity and credit dimension low at 33.32.

Breadth levels and trend remain healthy: 61.29% of constituents sit above their 200-day moving average and the new-lows ratio is only 1.29%; price is 7.10% above its 200-day average with 3-month momentum at 3.69%.
Sector breadth is good: 20 of 22 sectors/themes advanced, led by consumer electronics +4.95%, networking +3.58% and AI infrastructure +3.18%, with AMD up +2.57%.

contradicting_signals.claim: Cross-asset confirmation is only 0.50 on a flat trend, so equities, rates and volatility are not confirming each other: stocks rose while both the VIX and the 10-year yield moved higher.
Leadership is skewed to themes: consumer electronics +4.95% and networking +3.58% lead, while the mega-cap bellwether NVDA was only +0.02% and memory -0.35%; over one week NVDA is -4.39%.
Crypto did not follow the risk appetite: bitcoin traded at 77198.0, up only +0.06% on the day, while ether rose +3.26%, so the expansion in risk appetite is not broad-based.

what_changed_today: August CPI was released: 3.35% year over year (prior 3.30%) and core at 2.45% (prior 2.47%).
Yields stepped higher again: 10-year 4.83% (prior 4.80%), 2-year 4.43% (prior 4.39%) and the real rate 2.46% (prior 2.43%).
The VIX rose from 16.46 to 17.84, and the volatility dimension's trend shifted from flat to rising.
The total risk score is 45.21 with a one-day change of -0.44, keeping the caution and goldilocks combination; 20 of 22 themes advanced.
watch_next: Next week's Fed decision and the policy outcome: the market has already priced a hike (implied 4.08% versus an effective rate of 3.63%), so watch whether the language confirms it and whether the path shifts toward a stagflation narrative.
Advance Retail Sales on 2026-09-16 will test consumer resilience against rising inflation expectations.
FDX earnings on 2026-09-17 (forecast 4.21 usd) as an early read on real demand and freight volumes.
Middle East energy-transport risk: crude fell on Friday but posted sharp weekly gains and Brent net longs increased, so watch for further developments in Red Sea shipping and pipeline outages.

bull_case.title: Bull case: risk appetite persists once the hike lands
points: A 2.70% high-yield spread and a low-volatility backdrop point to limited systemic stress, with the index still closing higher under a priced-in hike.
Breadth is healthy (61.29% above the 200-day average) and 20 of 22 themes advanced; if the oil retreat continues, the inflation premium could ease.
The total risk score of 45.21 sits below the mid-range, the regime is still goldilocks, and the one-day change of -0.44 shows risk easing slightly.

base_case.title: Base case: a tighter macro anchor caps the upside
points: The macro dimension's 62.19 is the highest score and the real rate of 2.46% sits in the 99.6th percentile, so further upside needs financial conditions to ease.
The total risk score oscillates around 45 (one-day change -0.44, one-week change 2.04), keeping the caution stance.

bear_case.title: Bear case: a real-rate shock forces a valuation reset
points: If the 10-year yield keeps rising from 4.83% and the real rate breaks above 2.46%, discount pressure on high-multiple growth stocks intensifies.
Semis relative strength of -13.94 and a new-highs ratio of 1.94% show a fragile leadership base; if the VIX rises further from 17.84, breadth could deteriorate quickly.
Fiscal and energy pressure (a 1.96 trillion usd deficit over the first 11 months and diesel above 6 usd per gallon) may prolong inflation stickiness.
